Read every claim and all seven proof steps, with all 18 actual supplier clauses. Constant embedding is the supported-at-0 sequence, not coefficient extraction; the n=0 substitution map is the structure map R→A. Induction supplies finite multivariate coefficients and uniqueness, including the zero ring. Laurent convolution is over finite supports; finite Fubini proves associativity and the integer unit-power supplier proves unit substitution. Lexicographic order is total and translation invariant, including the singleton Z^0; the maximal-support coefficient has exactly one nonzero product, proving the domain claim. No domain or field assertion is made for zero/zero-divisor rings. Cross multiplication is transitive by nonzero-denominator cancellation; both operations respect it, the corrected addition identity is algebraically exact, common denominators give ring laws, and nonzero numerators invert. Thus both fraction-field embeddings are injective. Reader repairs are accepted: false constant map, false n=0 identity map, infinite-index convolution, wrong addition-compatibility computation, implicit ring-law closure, missing integer/unit prerequisites, and localization locator are corrected without weakening any claim. Source sections independently read: Bergman §4.12 pp.83–89 (polynomial and monoid-ring context), CRing Definitions13.1.2–13.1.4 pp.112–113 and Example13.1.7/Remark13.1.6 p.113; general localization uses an extra multiplier, while this local domain construction correctly cancels it.
